meta.note: Reader-facing one-sentence summaries for the 85 site stories whose summary was empty (76 twin-pass cards whose detector summary was the judge's reasoning and was removed, plus 9 Ketubot placeholders). Written by reading each story's William Davidson English (Hebrew alongside) in site/data on 2026-11-14; no model or API call. Only what the passage text supports. Keyed by site story id.

summaries.avodah_zarah-14b-7-7: Rav Dimi, arriving from Eretz Yisrael, explained the obscure mishnaic word naklas as koreyatei, and when Abaye protested that this was no clearer, Rav Dimi replied that in Eretz Yisrael people would understand it and show it to him.
summaries.avodah_zarah-65b-5-5: When a barrel of libation wine broke and spilled onto the dried figs Boethus ben Zunen was carrying on a ship, the Sages permitted the figs, because the wine spoiled their taste rather than improving it.
summaries.avodah_zarah-69a-1-1: Ravina held that vinegar must be 101 times a mouse's volume to cancel its flavor, as with teruma, and Rav Taḥlifa bar Giza challenged him that the case might be like a teruma spice, whose strong flavor is never cancelled.
summaries.bava_batra-30b-5-5: A man claimed land another held, saying the seller had robbed him of it; the possessor produced witnesses that the claimant had come at night offering to buy it, and Rava ruled that people pay to avoid a lawsuit.
summaries.bava_batra-8a-16-16: Rabba imposed a charity contribution on the orphans of the house of bar Maryon, and when Abaye objected that orphans are exempt, Rabba explained that he did it to raise their standing, not to benefit the poor.
summaries.bava_metzia-73a-9-9: Rava advised field guards who were paid from the harvest to help turn over the crops on the threshing floor, so their employment would last until the work was done and their reduced-rate payment would not count as interest.
summaries.bava_metzia-73b-2-2: Rava of Barnish pointed out to Rav Ashi that Sages paid for wine in Tishrei but chose it only in Tevet, gaining protection against spoiled wine, which he regarded as a form of interest.
summaries.bava_metzia-73b-6-6: Rav Pappa asked Rava about Sages who paid other people's head tax and then worked them hard, and Rava, glad to be asked while still alive, cited Rav Sheshet that by royal law non-payers must serve those who pay for them.
summaries.bava_metzia-85b-4-4: During their Torah debates, Rabbi Ḥanina boasted that if the Torah were forgotten he could restore it by his own reasoning, and Rabbi Ḥiyya answered that he was working to ensure it would never be forgotten at all.
summaries.bava_metzia-85b-7-7: Rabbi Zeira dreamed that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina told him where the Sages sit in the upper realms, and that Rabbi Yoḥanan could not be brought near Rabbi Ḥiyya amid its fiery sparks and burning fires.
summaries.beitzah-22a-16-16: Ameimar permitted treating a painful eye with ointment on the second day of Rosh HaShana, and when Rav Ashi objected, Ameimar said he followed the Sages of Neharde'a, since Elul had not been lengthened since the days of Ezra.
summaries.beitzah-25b-14-14: Ameimar and Mar Zutra were carried on their students' shoulders to the Festival lecture, either because they were afraid of falling or because they feared being crushed by the crowd.
summaries.berakhot-19a-9-9: Rabbi Yehuda denied that Akavya ben Mahalalel was ever excommunicated, saying it was Elazar ben Ḥanokh who was ostracized for demeaning handwashing, and that when he died the court placed a large stone on his coffin.
summaries.berakhot-30b-1-1: When Rabbi Ḥanina Kara, sitting before Rabbi Yannai, ruled according to Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, Rabbi Yannai told him to go read his verses outside, because the study hall did not accept that ruling.
summaries.berakhot-44a-4-4: Rav Dimi reported that King Yannai had a city on the King's Mountain that supplied six hundred thousand bowls of sardines each week to the workers cutting its figs.
summaries.berakhot-50a-13-13: Rava recalled that when the Sages ate at the Exilarch's house they recited Grace after Meals in groups of three, since a group of ten would anger the Exilarch and in the noise they could not hear his blessing.
summaries.chagigah-13a-10-10: A youth who expounded the electrum of the Divine Chariot was consumed by fire that came out, because his time to study such matters had not yet arrived.
summaries.chagigah-15a-10-10: Aḥer and Rabbi Meir debated a verse comparing Torah to gold and glass; when Aḥer cited Rabbi Akiva that a fallen scholar can be restored, Rabbi Meir urged him to repent, and Aḥer said a heavenly voice had excluded him.
summaries.chagigah-15a-7-7: After he had gone astray, Aḥer asked Rabbi Meir about the verse "God has made even the one as well as the other," and Rabbi Meir answered that God created a counterpart for everything, like mountains and hills, seas and rivers.
summaries.chagigah-15b-14-14: The philosopher Nimos HaGardi asked Rabbi Meir whether all wool that enters the dye vat comes out colored, and Rabbi Meir answered that only those who were pure from the start come out of Torah study worthy.
summaries.chagigah-5b-4-4: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya lay dying, the Sages asked who would answer the heretics once he was gone, and he replied from Jeremiah that when wisdom departs from Israel, the nations' wisdom vanishes as well.
summaries.chullin-124a-20-20: When Ulla confirmed that Rabbi Yoḥanan's ruling applied even to a piece of flesh the size of a sifter, Rav Naḥman swore that he would not have accepted it even from Rabbi Yoḥanan's own mouth.
summaries.chullin-128a-9-9: Rabbi Yehuda reports Rabbi Akiva's teaching that forbidden fat from an animal slaughtered in the villages becomes susceptible to impurity only once it is designated as food, since villagers with plenty of meat do not usually eat it.
summaries.chullin-50a-3-3: Rav Avya recalled standing before Rabbi Ami while the people there removed a handful of the fat on the bowstring and gave him the rest, which he ate, following the practice of Eretz Yisrael.
summaries.chullin-56a-10-10: Rav Naḥman challenged Rav Anan over the practice of Shmuel and Rav of inspecting by hand a bird bitten on the head by a weasel, and Rav Anan answered that Levi's contrary teaching refers to water birds, whose membrane is fragile.
summaries.eruvin-68a-2-2: Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan asked Abaye how an alleyway home to Rabba and Abaye could lack an eiruv, and Abaye explained that Rabba does not go around collecting, he himself is busy studying, and the other residents do not care.
summaries.ketubot-106a-2-3: Rav Anan sat in a box before Elijah until he had learned the whole Order of Elijah, and in a famine during Rav Yosef's years, Rav Yosef refused the Sages' plea to pray, pointing to the prophet Elisha, who did not pray either.
summaries.ketubot-112a-3-4: Seeing grape clusters as large as calves in Gavla, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi lamented that the land fed gentiles, and the next year, when Rabbi Ḥiyya admired clusters the size of goats, the locals told him to go away.
summaries.ketubot-54b-1-2: Rabbi Yoḥanan advised his relatives to have their father set aside land to support his wasteful wife, but after the father died Reish Lakish ordered them to support her fully, and Rabbi Yoḥanan said he could not overrule an equal.
summaries.ketubot-61b-1-1: A Roman ate peeled pomegranates in front of a woman who refused to marry him until she fell ill from craving them, then cured her, once she agreed to marry him, by having her spit out her saliva.
summaries.ketubot-63a-2-2: Rav Yosef son of Rava broke off his six years of study after three to visit his wife on the eve of Yom Kippur, and his father came out armed to confront him; in their quarrel neither ate the meal before the fast.
summaries.ketubot-69b-10-12: Passed over for head of the yeshiva, Ilfa hung from a ship's mast and vowed to fall if he could not trace any baraita of Rabbi Ḥiyya's school to a mishna, and he answered an elder's challenge about a dying father's weekly shekel.
summaries.ketubot-85a-3-4: Ḥama son of Rabba bar Abbahu paid the debt Avimi son of Rabbi Abbahu owed people from Bei Ḥozai, but they kept the debt document, claiming the money covered other debts, and Rabbi Abbahu ruled that they could.
summaries.ketubot-86a-4-4: In a similar case, Rafram pressed Rav Ashi to give a clear ruling, and Rav Ashi collected the full value of the debt written in the promissory note.
summaries.ketubot-91b-2-3: A debtor sold two mansions; when his creditor seized one and sought the other, the buyer offered him a thousand dinars to give up his claim, and Rava, rejecting Rami bar Ḥama's comparison, said refusing would be cruel.
summaries.makkot-16b-6-6: A man ate a fish-like creature found in the furrows of a plowed field, and Rav Yehuda had him flogged for eating a creeping animal.
summaries.megillah-28a-19-19: Avuh bar Ihi and Minyamin bar Ihi each claimed a blessing for himself, one for never gazing at a wicked gentile and the other for never going into partnership with one.
summaries.megillah-28a-5-5: Asked by his disciples how he merited long life, Rabbi Neḥunya ben HaKana said he never gained honor at another's expense, never went to bed with a grievance unresolved, and was always generous with his money.
summaries.megillah-28a-7-7: Each night before going to bed, Mar Zutra would say that he forgave anyone who had vexed him.
summaries.megillah-29a-4-4: Abaye always went in to pray at the ancient synagogues of Huzal and Neharde'a when he was nearby, and Shmuel's father and Levi, sitting in the Neharde'a synagogue, heard a loud sound as the Divine Presence came, and left.
summaries.moed_katan-12b-13-13: Rav permitted chopping down a palm tree on the intermediate days of a Festival even just for its sawdust, but Abaye cursed anyone who went to such effort for so small a need.
summaries.moed_katan-21a-6-6: When Rabbi Yosei's son died in Tzippori, Rabbi Yosei went into the study hall and taught there all day, although a mourner is normally barred from Torah study.
summaries.moed_katan-25b-2-2: When Ravina died, a eulogizer began by calling on the date palms to bow their heads for a righteous man like a palm, and to turn nights into days of weeping for one who studied through the night.
summaries.moed_katan-25b-9-9: When Rabbi Yoḥanan died, Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elazar opened his eulogy by saying the day was as hard for Israel as the day the sun set at noon, the verse Rabbi Yoḥanan had applied to King Josiah's death.
summaries.nedarim-49b-10-10: Rabbi Yehuda carried a pitcher on his shoulder to the study hall to sit on, and Rabbi Shimon carried a basket, each saying that labor is great because it brings honor to the one who does it.
summaries.niddah-24b-16-16: Abba Shaul, who had been a gravedigger, described what he saw in the bones of the dead: heavy drinkers of undiluted or diluted wine, and those who ate or drank too much, left burnt or black bones, while the moderate left marrow-full ones.
summaries.pesachim-101a-5-5: Abaye recalled that when Rabba recited kiddush he would tell his students to eat something there, since their lamps might go out before they reached their lodgings and kiddush counts only where one eats.
summaries.pesachim-49a-15-15: Rav Idi bar Avin married a priest's daughter and had two ordained sons, Rav Sheshet and Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rav Pappa said he became wealthy only because he too married a priest's daughter.
summaries.pesachim-51a-10-10: Rabba bar bar Ḥana, who had seen Rabbi Yoḥanan eat a certain fat, told his son, who lived in Babylonia, never to eat it, whether in his presence or not, since the son could not rely on his father's word alone.
summaries.pesachim-51a-2-2: When Yehuda and Hillel, sons of Rabban Gamliel, bathed together in Kabul, where brothers did not, the whole city denounced them, and Hillel slipped out to the outer chamber rather than tell them it was permitted.
summaries.pesachim-57a-7-7: Abba Shaul ben Batnit, quoting Abba Yosef ben Ḥanin, lamented the High Priestly families of Baitos, Ḥanin, Katros and Yishmael ben Piakhi for their clubs, whispers, lying pens and fists, while their relatives held the Temple offices.
summaries.pesachim-68b-12-12: Every thirty days Rav Sheshet reviewed what he had learned, then leaned against the door bolt and told his soul to rejoice, since it was for its sake that he had studied Scripture and Mishna.
summaries.rosh_hashanah-18a-7-7: Rabba and Abaye both descended from the house of Eli, whose members were cursed to die young; Rabba, who devoted himself to Torah, lived forty years, while Abaye, who added acts of kindness, lived sixty.
summaries.rosh_hashanah-25a-11-11: Rabbi Akiva found Rabbi Yehoshua distressed that Rabban Gamliel was forcing him to desecrate the day he reckoned as Yom Kippur, and Rabbi Yehoshua said it would be better to lie sick for a year than face such a decree.
summaries.sanhedrin-100a-5-5: When Rabbi Yirmeya taught before Rabbi Zeira that a river of delicacies will flow from the Holy of Holies, an elder praised him and cited Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rabbi Yirmeya asked whether such praise was the irreverence of an epikoros.
summaries.sanhedrin-104a-7-7: Rabbi Perida's grandfather found a skull near the gates of Jerusalem inscribed "This and yet another," and each time he buried it, it came back out of the grave.
summaries.sanhedrin-111a-3-3: When Rav Kahana, sitting before Rav, read Jeremiah's "one of a city, and two of a family" literally, Rav rebuked him just as Rabbi Yoḥanan had rebuked Reish Lakish: the merit of one benefits the whole city or family.
summaries.sanhedrin-11a-8-8: The Sages wished to eulogize Yehuda ben Bava as a pious and humble man, but the chance was lost, because he had been executed by the government and such men are not eulogized.
summaries.sanhedrin-29b-21-21: A court's document of admission bore only two signatures and did not mention a missing third judge, prompting Ravina, Rav Natan bar Ami and others to debate whether a proper court had issued it, until it was found to name Rabbana Ashi's court.
summaries.sanhedrin-38b-17-17: When Rabbi Akiva taught that one throne in Daniel's vision is for judgment and one for righteousness, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya told him to leave aggada for the laws of Nega'im and Oholot, and offered his own reading.
summaries.sanhedrin-39a-6-6: The emperor argued to Rabban Gamliel that different gods formed the mountains and created the wind, and Rabban Gamliel replied that Adam too is described as both created and formed, yet no one says two gods made him.
summaries.sanhedrin-39a-7-7: Continuing their debate, Rabban Gamliel asked the emperor whether separate gods made the eye and the ear, and when the emperor said yes, asked whether all those gods agree when the moment of death arrives.
summaries.sanhedrin-52b-3-3: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok recalled a priest's daughter who committed adultery being executed by actual burning, and the Sages told him the court then was not proficient; Rav Yosef says it was a Sadducee court.
summaries.shabbat-115b-1-1: When Rabbi Yishmael climbed a ladder in Sidon to confront a man writing blessings, the scribe sank the bundle in a basin of water, and Rabbi Yishmael told him that destroying them was worse than writing them.
summaries.shabbat-156a-4-4: Ze'eiri's notebook records that he asked Rabbi Ḥiyya whether one may knead on Shabbat or move fodder from one animal to another, followed by rulings from Rav Menashya, Rav Yosef and Ulla on how much fodder may be added.
summaries.shabbat-23b-3-3: Seeing Rabbi Avin the carpenter kindle many Shabbat lights, Rav Huna foretold that two great men would come from his house, and his sons Rav Idi and Rav Ḥiyya did; Rav Ḥisda likewise foresaw Rav Sheizvi from his father's lamps.
summaries.sukkah-26a-6-6: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel recalled that when his eyes hurt in Caesarea, Rabbi Yosei ben Ḥalafta allowed him and his attendant to sleep outside the sukka.
summaries.sukkah-28a-3-3: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai never spoke idly, never walked four cubits without Torah and phylacteries, was always first in the study hall and opened the door for his students himself, and his student Rabbi Eliezer modeled himself on him.
summaries.sukkah-53a-2-2: While rejoicing at the Celebration of the Drawing of the Water, Hillel the Elder would say, "If I am here, everyone is here," and that his feet carried him to the place he loved.
summaries.taanit-21b-8-8: When told that locusts had come but were eating very little, Rav Yehuda decreed a fast anyway, asking whether the locusts had brought their own provisions.
summaries.taanit-23b-8-8: Rabbi Zerika told Rav Safra how the pious men of Babylonia, Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda, would gather publicly to pray for rain, in contrast to the powerful men of Eretz Yisrael.
summaries.taanit-28a-6-6: The Sages ask who were the descendants of those who deceived the authorities with a pestle and of those who packed dried figs, families who brought wood to the Temple on the fifteenth of Av.
summaries.yevamot-105a-13-13: Rabba and Abaye, descendants of the house of Eli, outlived that family's curse of early death: Rabba, who devoted himself to Torah study, lived forty years, and Abaye, who added acts of kindness, lived sixty.
summaries.yevamot-121b-14-14: Hearing a gentile call out that Ḥivvai had died, Rav Yosef allowed Ḥivvai's wife to remarry, and when another gentile lamented a dead horseman of Pumbedita, Rav Yosef, or some say Rava, let his wife remarry too.
summaries.yevamot-34b-6-6: Rava told his wife, Rav Ḥisda's daughter, that the Sages were gossiping because she bore him children after more than ten years of widowhood, and she answered that her mind had always been on him.
summaries.yevamot-42b-8-8: When Rabbi Zerika asked Rabbi Abbahu about a contradiction, Rabbi Abbahu replied that whoever raised it was careless with his flour, and explained the rule for an unattributed ruling followed by a dispute.
summaries.yevamot-63a-6-6: Seeing a field plowed across its width, Rabbi Elazar told it that even if it were plowed lengthwise as well, business would still pay better than farming it.
summaries.yoma-19b-5-5: When Rav Ḥanan bar Rava taught the name Zekharya ben Kefutal, Rav showed with a hand gesture that it should be pronounced Kevutal, because he was reciting Shema and could not speak.
summaries.yoma-35b-5-5: In the Heavenly court, a poor man who excuses his neglect of Torah by his poverty is asked whether he was any poorer than Hillel, who was wretchedly poor and still sought to study.
summaries.yoma-38b-2-2: Ben Kamtzar could write a four-letter word at once with four quills between his fingers but refused to teach the skill, and unlike others who guarded their techniques, he had no reason but his own honor.
summaries.yoma-77b-9-9: Rav Yosef allowed villagers of Bei Tarbu to wade through water to his Yom Kippur lecture but not back home, and Abaye warned this would stop them coming; in another version, Rav Yosef allowed both for that very reason.
summaries.yoma-78a-9-9: Rabba bar Mari reported how a wet cloth is prepared in Eretz Yisrael for the Ninth of Av and for Yom Kippur, and Rabbi Ya'akov told Rabbi Yirmeya bar Taḥlifa that he had reported the two days the other way round.
summaries.yoma-79a-1-1: On Sukkot, when Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai was brought a cooked dish to taste and Rabban Gamliel two dates and a tankard of water, both asked for the food to be taken up to the sukka, choosing to be strict with themselves.
summaries.yoma-83b-9-9: Rabbi Yoḥanan recalled that when he was seized with bulmos, a ravenous faintness, he ran to the east side of a fig tree, found ripe figs there and ate them, fulfilling the verse that wisdom preserves life.
summaries.yoma-87a-14-14: When someone insulted Rabbi Zeira, he would pace back and forth in front of that person, making it easy for him to come and apologize.
